feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector leadership: clear positioning, relevant scope, and good evidence of progression and ownership. It reads professionally, but it is slightly repetitive, a bit dense, and could sharpen impact by adding more outcomes and trimming overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior narrative: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support the “digital platform and communications systems leader” positioning.  
- Good credibility signals: named platforms, scale metrics, governance scope, and concrete projects make the experience believable and substantive.  
- Writing is polished overall: tone is consistent, action-oriented, and largely free of grammar or spelling errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add stronger results language: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma, and punctuation/hyphenation style varies slightly across sections. No major misspellings found; grammar is strong overall.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “driving” enterprise digital platforms, governance, and content operations.
- Add one concrete proof point from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas: web modernization, analytics, editorial governance, and multimedia/AI experiences.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Built and scaled digital ecosystems including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” repeats the subtitle’s leadership positioning.
- The long list of capabilities overlaps with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize leadership-level capability areas rather than repeating detailed skill phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Recast as broader, executive-level competency labels: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and content operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “systems,” “operations,” and “experiences” unless they add clear distinction.
- Consider replacing “editorial systems” with “content operations” for clearer alignment with the experience section.
- Use “search and discovery” instead of “search and content experiences” for sharper, more natural phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” also repeats detail already covered in Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and making outcomes or scope more concrete would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise achievement, not a mini paragraph.
- Use parallel verbs and cleaner phrasing: “Created AI-enabled legislative search using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Replace vague terms like “improve discovery” and “designed for continued campaign growth” with clearer value, scale, or audience impact where possible.
- Standardize style: use “10 x 20-foot” (not 10×20-foot) and keep capitalization/tense consistent across all four entries.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with current freelance and NACo bullets; consider framing these as “Selected projects” with distinct outcomes or omitting the most repetitive one.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most additive because it introduces archival media and conference display work not emphasized elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-driven achievement entry. Tighten phrasing and foreground the highest-impact work, especially systems, Drupal delivery, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Open with outcome + client context: “Lead digital strategy, web operations, and platform improvements for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one sharper line: “Built cross-functional content workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet more concise and active: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and downloadable member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public sites.”
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing time reduced, toolkit downloads, search success rate, or engagement gains from the AI-enabled search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “digital systems” repeat themes already covered heavily in the NACo roles—use this entry to emphasize consulting impact and AI/search leadership.
- Avoid overexplaining CMS/front-end skills already listed in Topline Skills/Technical sections.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation wins, and add outcome language beyond platform scope.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize 3–5 strongest wins and start with action + result: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible for studio/analytics/governance work: cost savings, faster production, improved reporting cadence, reduced publishing bottlenecks, stronger engagement, or better decision-making.
- Tighten softer bullets: e.g., “Established publishing governance, editorial standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and operational efficiency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, transformation, and infrastructure.
- Video leadership also appears in earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the in-house studio, not recurring video production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about execution, channel ownership, and editorial operations rather than broad digital leadership.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed day-to-day execution of NACo’s digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy and member communications.”
- Make workflow/editorial bullets more concrete: “Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving publishing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director role; avoid repeating “led/oversaw” language.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the format.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing enterprise scope, governance, and mission-driven communications.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with tighter, higher-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Keep terminology consistent with recent experience: use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel,” and “content operations” to echo current consulting/NACo work.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-traffic, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” repeats language already used in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is broad and may duplicate “editorial workflow design” and “multi-channel communication” elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, make it more outcome-oriented and emphasize the most relevant, recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and CMS modernization” instead of listing platforms without context.
- Prioritize recent/high-value items from current roles: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Tighten older or lower-signal items: replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript)” and consider dropping jQuery.
- Possible rewrite: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & front-end implementation • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save detailed tools there.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies/Technical + IT, so avoid repeating exact phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. Tightening it around decision-making and optimization would better reflect the impact shown in the 2022–present experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis”
- Group platforms more cleanly: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery, KPI design, executive dashboards, SEO/performance analysis”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to outcomes in experience bullets instead of here: reporting adoption, improved decision-making, traffic/conversion gains, or governance improvements

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies; “executive dashboards” or “decision-support reporting” is sharper
- Tool names here also repeat the NACo Director bullet; keep this section concise and let the work experience carry impact

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with stronger evidence already shown in recent NACo roles. Make it more specific to senior-level capability and emphasize production environments you’ve actually led.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, higher-value phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera operation,” “Studio build-out and operations,” “Virtual event production.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera systems • Studio build-out and operations • Virtual event production”
- If space allows, add one scale cue tied to recent work, e.g. “in-house studio operations” or “recurring advocacy programming,” to reinforce credibility.
- Keep wording consistent with the rest of the CV: use “hybrid event delivery” or “event production,” not both.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; consider simplifying one of the two.
- “Video production” and “studio operations” are already evidenced in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid expanding this into a long list.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” For a recent, senior profile, this item should either be more selective or add context on level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to the platforms most central to recent work: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages”
- Drop GitHub Pages unless it was used meaningfully in recent roles; it feels lower-impact than the others.
- If space allows, add proficiency/context instead of a bare list: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages”
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest relevance: Drupal first, then WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; avoid repeating the exact same list in both places.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so this item should add specificity, not restate breadth.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It would be stronger if grouped by level/relevance and framed around current, applied tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for clarity and recency: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations & tagging: API integrations, Google Tag Manager • Deployment & automation: GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- Put the most relevant/current tools first based on recent roles: API integrations, GTM, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers, then front-end languages.
- If accurate, add one brief qualifier elsewhere in the CV tying these to outcomes, e.g., “used for CMS enhancements, tagging, deployment automation, and lightweight web tooling.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; keep one version broader and this one strictly tool-based.
- “API integrations” and “workflow automation” are already implied in other skills sections—avoid repeating both in multiple places.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize function, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Tighten and group by use case: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If accurate, add light context instead of just listing tools: “Used to build editorial workflows, automate handoffs/notifications, and coordinate cross-team publishing operations.”
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first; consider dropping weaker/older items if not used recently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep only if they support a workflow/operations narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it’s too bare and undersells a clear strength shown in recent roles: managing enterprise email/newsletter operations. Reframe it to emphasize campaign and membership communications systems rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform names for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope/context instead of a pure list, e.g.: Enterprise email, newsletter, and member engagement platforms: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If one platform was primary in recent work, order by strongest/recentest use rather than alphabetically.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work experience already showing email leadership; avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here unless tied to a specific platform.
- “Engagement Systems” is vague and may duplicate broader digital strategy language elsewhere.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it into a cleaner technical list and emphasize methods/tools rather than broad capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting
- Swap “SEO” for “Google Search Console” if you want this section to stay tool-focused; keep SEO in Core Competencies/Topline Skills instead.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “Performance reporting” for a sharper, outcome-linked phrase.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this one purely tools-based.
- “A/B testing” is not evidenced elsewhere in recent roles; keep only if you can support it in experience bullets.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and the website refresh.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted through two digital roles while helping build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website refresh size/traffic impact, livestream/event volume, video cadence, or team/process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with concrete actions such as “produced weekly video updates, managed livestreams, and supported a major website refresh.”
- Consider: “Produced recurring video and livestream content, supported a major website refresh, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the later “weekly advocacy video update”; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats themes covered more strongly in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and trim broad support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the standout result: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific verb: “Produced multimedia and digital content supporting program communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes, audience, stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item anchored in innovation/research + first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating team-building or video/livestream themes already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” and “Video production and editing / Studio operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize software/tool proficiency rather than broad capabilities already proven in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Tools
- Replace with: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want one capability phrase, keep only one specific add-on: Livestream production workflows
- Consider moving “Podcast production” out unless you can quantify it elsewhere; it reads more like a function/accomplishment than a tool

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” duplicates Topline Skills (“Livestreaming,” “Studio operations,” “Hybrid and virtual event production”)
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older work experience; keeping it here may overstate older experience versus more recent digital leadership strengths
